Present the list in alphabetical order by first name.

**Susan Kare** ( _KAIR_; born February 5, 1954) is an American artist and graphic designer, who contributed interface elements and typefaces for the first Apple Macintosh personal computer from 1983 to 1986.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susan_Kare#cite_note-Design_Biography-4) She was employee #10 and creative director at NeXT, the company formed by Steve Jobs after he left Apple in 1985. She has worked as a design consultant to Microsoft, IBM, Sony Pictures, Facebook, and Pinterest. As of November 2026, Kare is a partner at Kare Prints.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susan_Kare#cite_note-:0-5) As a pioneer of pixel art and of the graphical computer interface, she has been celebrated as one of the most significant designers of modern technology.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susan_Kare#cite_note-6)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susan_Kare#cite_note-MICG-2022-3)

## Early life and education
[edit]
Kare was born in Ithaca, New York to Jewish-American parents.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susan_Kare#cite_note-7) Her father was a professor at the University of Pennsylvania and director of the Monell Chemical Senses Center, a research facility for the senses of taste and smell.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susan_Kare#cite_note-Regional-8) Her mother taught her counted-thread embroidery[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susan_Kare#cite_note-How_Susan-2) as she immersed herself in drawings, paintings, and crafts.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susan_Kare#cite_note-Iconic_Iconographer_Priceonomics-9) Her brother was aerospace engineer Jordin Kare.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susan_Kare#cite_note-hom_su-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susan_Kare#cite_note-11) She graduated from Harriton High School in 1971. She graduated _summa cum laude_ with a B.A. in art from Mount Holyoke College in 1975, with an undergraduate honors thesis on mathematics_[citation needed_]. She received an M.A. and a Ph.D. in fine arts from New York University in 1978 with a doctoral dissertation on "the use of caricature in selected sculptures of Honoré Daumier and Claes Oldenburg". Her goal was "to be either a fine artist or teacher".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susan_Kare#cite_note-hom_su-10)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susan_Kare#cite_note-I.D._Forty-12)

**Archie Boston Jr.** (born 1943) is an American graphic artist, and retired professor.
Born to an impoverished family in a small town in southern Florida,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Boston_Jr.#cite_note-Rapp-2008-1) Boston received an education in graphic design[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Boston_Jr.#cite_note-Tampa_Bay_Times-1972-2) at Chouinard Art Institute located in Los Angeles.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Boston_Jr.#cite_note-Rapp-2008-1) During school and after graduation, he worked in numerous ad agencies based in Los Angeles[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Boston_Jr.#cite_note-AIGA-3) before forming Boston & Boston Design with his brother Bradford in 1967—one of the first Black-owned agencies in the United States.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Boston_Jr.#cite_note-Rapp-2008-1)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Boston_Jr.#cite_note-AIGA-3) In 1972, at age 29, he became the president of the Art Director Club of Los Angeles, the second-largest in the nation. He was the first Black president in the organization's 28-year history.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Boston_Jr.#cite_note-Tampa_Bay_Times-1972-2)

In 1977 Boston received a master's degree from the University of Southern California, and began his long career as an educator[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Boston_Jr.#cite_note-Rubenstein_Rare_Book-4) at California State University, Long Beach.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Boston_Jr.#cite_note-Rapp-2008-1) He helped found the Visual Communications Design program there and served as the department chair.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Boston_Jr.#cite_note-Rapp-2008-1)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Boston_Jr.#cite_note-AIGA-3) In 2004 he was named Outstanding Professor of the Year.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Boston_Jr.#cite_note-Eye_on_Design-2021-5)
He has produced several documentary films, including _20 Outstanding Los Angeles Designers_[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Boston_Jr.#cite_note-AIGA-3) and, in 2018 with his brother David, he produced the documentary, _Black Pioneers of the Sunshine City_ about the activist members of the Black community in St. Petersburg, Florida[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Boston_Jr.#cite_note-WFLA-2018-6)
In 2021, Boston became an American Institute of Graphic Arts medalist.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archie_Boston_Jr.#cite_note-AIGA-2-7)
